overview:
The claim of this chapter, "the big statement" of these classes, is that the *hishtalshelus* is not a machine. When you contemplate the lights and vessels of *Atzilus* in detail, the main point is *ihu v'chayohi chad*, *ihu v'garmohi chad*: G-d is one with the vessels just as with the lights, because He chose both. The root of the vessels, the *reshimu* and the simple matter that comes before the form, is even before the root of the lights.

To show it, the Mitteler Rebbe distinguishes two kinds of limit. A *gvul b'koach*, like the hand's power of movement, is spiritual, essential and a freedom; a *gvul b'poel*, the throw once thrown, is physical and only one thing. The vessels of *Atzilus* are only a limit in potential, and the One who wills is the one who limits the will, like a person refusing a sardine sandwich. So the money that comes through *chesed* is His choice too, and the *kavanos* in prayer point to Him. In their root the roles reverse: what is limited as revealed spreads in the source, like the Rebbe in his room.

sections.summary: The main point of contemplating the lights and vessels of *Atzilus* in detail is that G-d is one with the vessels just as He is one with the lights. The root of the vessels is even before the root of the lights: something has to make the light stop and take a form, and that is the simple matter that comes before the form.

blocks.text:
**However, when you're going to do hisbonenus** (contemplation) **in the oros and kelim** (the lights and vessels) **of Atzilus** (the world of Emanation) **in a more particular way**, the main thing is not all the stuff explained so far: how the lights become limited in the vessels and change their *mahus* (nature) from spiritual to physical. That is the general idea, just to understand what goes on.

In a particular *hisbonenus* the main thing is *ihu v'chayohi chad*, *ihu v'garmohi chad*: just as G-d is one with the lights, the life force, He is one with the vessels, the body.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: In general the vessels relate to the light as the last few chapters described. But in a particular *hisbonenus* the main thing is to realize that their limitation comes straight from G-d, who chooses it with a *bechira chofshis* (free choice). So it is a revelation of His *etzem* (essence) and His *kol yachol*-ness (His being all-powerful) just as much as the light is. Just as *ihu v'chayohi chad*, so too *ihu v'garmohi chad*.

blocks.text:
**Even though the lights are b'li ma** (without a what), **and the vessels are already like a tangible, concrete thing that is limited**, it seems the infinite lights reveal G-d better. "So no, it's not really true."

From the side of the *Atzmus haMaatzil* (the Essence of the Emanator), the root of the vessels came first: the lights come from the *Kav* (the ray of light), the vessels from the *reshimu* (the impression left after the *tzimtzum*), and the *reshimu* is before the *Kav*. G-d revealing Himself in a limited way is in a way a higher revelation than His being "just infinite, transcendental, great, unknowable beyond."

phrases.en: from the fact that from the thickening of the light comes the vessel,

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text:
This is apparent **from the fact that from the thickening of the light comes the vessel**: **there has to be something before that.** The light thickens, but what makes it thicken? Shine a light and it keeps going straight. What makes it stop and turn and get a form?

Say G-d reveals Himself as infinite light above all limitations, which becomes a vessel only when it comes into a particular revelation. What made it go into *chesed* (kindness)? Into *chachma* (wisdom)? Into any vessel? There must be a higher thing, *mamash* (actually) G-d choosing to reveal Himself in a particular form, stronger than the light because it forces the light into that form: "the boss of the light", that tells the light what to do.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: We see that in the body, which is a separate existence from the soul. And the power of sight is in a way made of the limited things it sees: being a power of sight means that it can see those things.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.en: or the *chomer hiyuli*,

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.en: which goes before the form.

blocks.text: **And this source for the vessel that comes before the light is called the simple chomer** (matter), **or the chomer hiyuli** (the raw, formless matter), **which goes before the form**, because the form is given to that matter. The soul gives the body its form, which is the thickening of the light, but the physical matter is there before, and the soul just forms it. As said before, the outside world already has its limitations, and when your *ratzon* (will) meets it, it comes out a certain way. It has a separate source: the form is not coming totally from the light.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: A cup to drink water
blocks.text:
Say you want a cup. What you really want is to drink water. How does that *ratzon* get the form of a cup? In the world water has to be held in something waterproof, shaped so the water goes in and does not come out. The shape of the cup is your *ratzon* to drink water made tangible, practical in the world: that is the thickening of the light.

But it already presupposes the properties of water, and of the ceramics or plastic you make the cup out of. Those building blocks are there, and you just put the form together from the definitions that already exist.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: The seed and the power of growth
blocks.text: So the light needs some limitations to work with, or it would never come out one way over another. Like the power of growth: it needs the seed, whose limitations tell it how to grow, or it would never get thickened into a certain tree. You need something to be *metzamtzem* (contract, limit) it, and what limits it comes from a higher source, in a way a separate thing.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: The same when the soul comes into the body: it gives the body its form and its life, but the body already has "the DNA and whatever", which has a form of its own. That is what it explains in certain places: we say the vessel comes from the thickening of the light, but it really comes from the light hitting against the *chomer hapashut*, the simple matter.

audio.lecture: 57 - Chap- 29-1 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: Two reference points
blocks.text: There is the *chomer hapashut*, the *hiyuli* of the *reshimu*, and there is the *hiyuli* of the *Kav*; when the two hit against each other, they are synthesized into a certain vessel. Two reference points intersect at only one point, so they define where they meet. With one reference point you cannot start to define anything, because it could be anything. Now he explains something slightly related, which will connect back to this.

blocks.title: I don't want no sardine sandwich
blocks.text:
"I'm hungry, I want something to eat."

"Okay, here's a sardine sandwich."

"Well, I don't want no sardine sandwich."

"What? You said you wanted something to eat. It should extend to anything."

"No. The same way that I say that I want it, I can say that I don't want it."

That is the power of *ratzon*: one power, to come out of yourself and want it, as much or as little as you choose, or not at all.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: Once you make a limitation, it can come into *chachma*. With a clear definition of what you want and what you do not, you can say what you want; you have a certain *chachma*, a picture of it: "I want a peanut butter and jelly sandwich." That is still a general limitation, because you did not say which peanut butter and jelly sandwich: it is a general picture.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: "This one's mine"
blocks.text:
Or, if you want to be stubborn: "I want that one." "Which one? I have two." "That one." "So you want this one?" "No, I want that one."

Rabbi Walters' nephew does that. He wants things to be his, so when his mother lights candles for *Shabbos*, he says, "This one's mine and this one's my brother's." "What's the difference? They're exactly the same." "No, this one's mine." You can decide that, and not want the other one.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text:
Or you keep it general: "I just want a candle. I don't care which one." You can be as particular or as non-particular as you want: "something to eat, I don't care what, as long as it's edible", or you *davka* (specifically) want this and nothing else.

The point is that the limitation comes from you, just like the desire. It is not that you have a desire for food and your body processes it like a machine into wanting a certain thing. First of all, you do not have to want food; you choose to want it. And as you choose the desire, which is why it comes from your *etzem*, by *bechira* (choice), you choose the limitation.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.en: once you limit it then you can have a reason for the *ratzon*.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: שאם לא היה פוסק כח ואור הרצון,
phrases.en: if the light of the desire wouldn't stop,

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: לא היה בא לעולם לכלל טעם לרצון
phrases.en: it could never come to a reason.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **Once you limit it then you can have a reason for the ratzon**, because **if the light of the desire wouldn't stop, it could never come to a reason.** Having a reason means you want it because it has a certain thing, and that already limits it: you want it for a certain general characteristic.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: Chocolate, or the one in the right hand
blocks.text: Two flavors of ice cream. "I want this one." "Why?" "Because it's chocolate." That is a reason, so it can come into a *chachma*: "Oh, so you like chocolate." There is already a *sechel* (intellect) to figure out what to get you. Or another reason: "It's not because it's chocolate. I always take the things on the right side, and you're holding that one in your right hand." Then it has nothing to do with the flavor.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: But "I just want it because I want it" does not come into a *sechel* at all, because your *ratzon* is not stopping or connecting to any particular thing; it stays on the level of *ratzon*: "I want whatever I want, and that's it." You did not limit it. Once you are *metzamtzem* it to "I want this," you can come to a *sechel*, a picture of what you want: it becomes a matter and a reason for the will.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

sections.title: The kav hamida makes every limit and is not limited: the vessels are no machine
sections.summary: The *kav hamida*, the measuring stick that can measure any size, makes every actual limit in the lights and in the vessels, yet is itself no limit: G-d chooses the light and also the vessel. Like a language or a law kept by convention, the vessels only seem to run by themselves; money is a vessel for *chesed* only because He chose it.

phrases.en: this limitation is all from the *maamar* of the *kav hamida*,

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: העושה כל גבול בפועל ממש באורות
phrases.en: this is what makes every limitation in the lights, that it makes the light come out *davka* a certain way.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **This limitation is all from the maamar** (the saying) **of the kav hamida** (the line of measure): you measure out how your *ratzon* will come out, how much, where it stops and in which way. As explained before, the *kav hamida* is a potential limitation: the same measuring stick measures out any size you want, so a general system of measurement does not limit you. "And the same power that lets you make the rules lets you break the rules," as we said in chapter 15. **This is what makes every limitation in the lights, that it makes the light come out davka a certain way.**

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: וכך הוא עושה כל גבול בפועל ממש בכלים
phrases.en: and it also makes every limitation in the vessels,

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: דעשר ספירות המגבילים, איך שיגבילו בפועל ממש
phrases.en: how they will limit it.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: אבל מקור ושרש שלהם אינו בחינת גבול אמיתי,
phrases.en: but the source, in other words the *Kav* itself, the power of the *Kav*, is not a real *gvul*,

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: רק שהוא עושה את אופן ההגבלה
phrases.en: it's just that it makes the limitation.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **And it also makes every limitation in the vessels**: by the *kav hamida* you have a *ratzon*, say to reveal yourself as kind, and it also chooses how you express the kindness. You choose both. **But the source, in other words the Kav itself, the power of the Kav, is not a real gvul**; it defines the limit but is not limited itself. On the contrary, you have free choice to limit however you want.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: Until now it may have sounded otherwise. The Arizal's *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent) talks about the light, not the vessels, so it sounds as if the vessels are already set up: you choose how the lights come out, and the vessels automatically limit them and make them physical and tangible. As if once G-d chose to reveal Himself through *chesed*, it automatically gets thickened into this world, or into the ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes). "But it's not really like that, you know, at all." There is no point where it becomes a mechanistic thing, where G-d has to do it a certain way.

audio.lecture: 58 - Chap- 29-2 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: The rules of a language
blocks.text: It is like a language. Once the rules are set, this word means this and that word means that, a *ratzon* to say something, which is like a light, has to come out in certain words: to say apple, you say apple. But besides choosing what to say, you choose to set up the language that way, and you can change it. Once the vessels are chosen, they seem to act like a machine: plug in a light and it comes out automatically. "But it's really an illusion": you have poetic license, and you keep it up all the time, by convention.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.outOfPlace: Class 59 opens by continuing the explanation of line 25 from the end of class 58, before it reads line 26.

blocks.text: It is like what was said way back about laws. There is an illusion that the laws are a set thing separate from you, and everything filters through them automatically, like a machine. But you choose all the time to uphold them, to interpret them a certain way by convention, and to keep that conservative consistency. They do not control you.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: Chesed means He gives me money
blocks.text:
In the same way the vessels make no limitation or control on G-d, even though once He chose to reveal Himself a certain way, it looks automatic. "Oh, if G-d wants to reveal *chesed*, He gives me money. And if G-d wants to reveal *gevura* (might, restraint), He doesn't give me money." Why? Because the light of *chesed* in the vessel of *chesed* turns into money. So G-d only chooses the light, and the vessel channels it automatically into something physical, and that is set.

But the vessels are also not set. Money is not inherently a *chesed*; it is one only because He chose to make it the vessel for *chesed*, and if He wants, He can make it a *gevura* vessel. G-d controls both halves; both are in a way just as infinite, both just from His choice.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: That is why nature is really higher than nature, and higher than nature is really nature. The vessel is just as infinite as the light: it seems a nature, a set thing, but it comes by G-d's choice too. And the light is just as much a nature and a limitation as the vessel: G-d chose to reveal Himself as transcendent and infinite, but to Him that is just as limited as the vessels.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: What money really is
blocks.text:
It depends how low a vessel you mean: the power of creating, or money. The vessel of *chesed* is the power to give life and to create, and money is just a *levush* (garment) for it, a vessel in *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* (the worlds of Creation, Formation and Action). The concept of money is like *Yetzira*, the actual currency is in *Asiya*; you do not need physical bills and coins.

A person being wealthy is not really a real thing; people just know he has the money. "Like Bill Gates, for example. He doesn't really have the money." He owns a company and houses. Even what is in your bank is only in theory yours. The *Asiya* thing is something tangible: "cash, cold cash." And even that only represents something: that is the *kli* (vessel) alone. That is part of what he explains now.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

sections.title: The power to contract is equal to the power to spread: the reshimu and the Kav
sections.summary: The limit comes from the *gevura* of the *Ein Sof*, the power to contract, which is as infinite as the power to spread, because one who can do anything can also limit. The *reshimu* is G-d's ability to reveal something set and separate, the root of the vessels; the *Kav*, the root of the lights, is His conscious control of that separate thing.

phrases.en: which this limitation comes from the *kav hamida*,

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **Which this limitation comes from the kav hamida, from the power of gevura of the Ein Sof** (the Infinite), the power to contract, equal to the power to extend: both are infinite, **two equal, opposite sides**, **because if G-d can do anything, then that includes also the ability to make any limitation.** Whoever can do whatever he wants can be as infinite or as limited as he wants.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.title: The throw and the light switch
blocks.text: Just like your hand: if you can throw as hard as you want, you can throw as soft as you want. "It's a two-way street." A light switch turns on and off; the power to turn it on means you do not have to. So G-d's power of being infinite means He does not have to be infinite, or else it would be an essential limitation.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: We are not saying that G-d is essentially an infinite being; He has the power of infinity, which means He also has the power of finitude. If G-d cannot limit Himself, He must have a bigger G-d telling Him what to do. "You go tell him that he can't do it. If G-d wants to limit himself, you go tell him that, no, you can't do it, I'm sorry."

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.question: Can G-d make a rock He cannot lift: can He make Himself limited and nothing else?
blocks.text: If G-d *mamash* made Himself limited, so that is all He is, ever was and ever will be, you are already going out of the *hishtalshelus*, where human intellect cannot follow. In our *hishtalshelus* G-d is revealed through *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon* (single, one and original): *davka* in all three together do we see the *Atzmus Ein Sof*; that is the first *tzimtzum* (contraction). Whatever lacks the three together does not make sense to us as G-d. We know it must be so, but we cannot talk about it. Nevertheless, it is true. So the answer is yes, He could, and He could lift it anyway, "and whatever." "Things do not have to make sense to us."

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: As explained elsewhere, and **we explained before** (in chapter 15, he thinks, or later): **the power of limitation in the Ein Sof is the reshimu**, its revelation, the root of the limitation of the vessels of *Atzilus*: **the power of limitation in the ten sefiros is coming from the reshimu.** The *reshimu* is G-d's ability to reveal Himself as something separate from Himself, no longer connected to a *bechira*: it just is what it is, set.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **And from the Kav**: G-d's ability to reveal Himself through control of something separate from Him. The light before the *tzimtzum* reveals that there is only G-d, who can do whatever He wants, unlimited. The *reshimu* is His ability to reveal something set and limited, that appears separate and is not connected to choice anymore. The *Kav* is the intermediate that connects the two: G-d's infinite control, controlling that separate, limited thing however He wants.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: Like your soul in your body: the body is a separate, limited thing, but the soul goes into it and controls it, and they become connected. The *Kav*, **which comes from the reshimu**: **that's the source of all the lights.** The lights come from the way G-d chooses to control the *kelim* (vessels), **as explained elsewhere at length.**

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

sections.title: So He and His organs are one: even the vessels of Atzilus are only a limit in potential
sections.summary: The names *Ayin Beis* and *SaG*, the vessels of *Atzilus*, limit only because G-d chose it, so He is one with them as with the lights; they are a limit in potential, and only in *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* is there an actual limit. So the *hishtalshelus* is no machine, and one who has the names in mind in prayer has in mind the One who chooses to use them.

phrases.en: if so,

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: גם שבחינת הכלים דאצילות מגבילים ממש
phrases.en: even though the vessels of *Atzilus* actually limit the light,

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.en: which is the idea of the names of *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH*, *BaN*,

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.en: which are called letters,

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: הרי אין זה רק מצד כח העושה לגבול זה בעצמות המאציל
phrases.en: these limitations are coming from the power that makes it; in other words, that G-d chose that it should come out in this way.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.en: and this is why we say that He and His organs are one,

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.en: because they're coming from the *koach* of the *Ein Sof* itself,

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: כמו דאיהו וחיוהי חד בבחינת האורות כו'
phrases.en: just like He is one with the lights.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **If so, even though the vessels of Atzilus actually limit the light, which is the idea of the names of Ayin Beis, SaG, MaH, BaN** (the Names of seventy-two, sixty-three, forty-five and fifty-two), **which are called letters**, G-d revealed as a certain wisdom, like the Written Torah, "that's it, that's the Torah": still, G-d chose that it should come out this way, from His very essence. So that too reveals His *etzem*: He *mamash* chose it.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **And this is why we say that He and His organs are one**: the vessels are one with G-d too, **because they're coming from the koach** (the power) **of the Ein Sof itself**, from G-d being *kol yachol*, who chose them; **just like He is one with the lights**, because He chose them. There is *mamash* no difference as far as the connection to the *etzem* goes.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: Within our *hishtalshelus* the *tzimtzum* is not *kipshuto* (literal): G-d always has the infinite ability of before the *tzimtzum*, and only makes it look limited. Or switch it around: the limitations always exist, and the choice just reveals certain ones of them. Either way, that is the *etzem d'Ein Sof*, the *gilui* (revelation) of the *Atzmus*.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: The *Atzmus* cannot even be revealed, let alone pick up a rock or not. "What's *Atzmus* good for anyway, you know?" It is *ilu yedativ hayisiv* (if I knew Him, I would be Him): you would have to be it to know it. What comes out is the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light), the *or hamispashet* that spreads out, not the *etzem d'Ein Sof*. That it can be revealed, and that you are it, is a *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching) thing: *chakira* (philosophical inquiry) says you cannot; *Chassidus* says you can.

audio.lecture: 59 - Chap- 29-3 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: (ובאמת גם בחינת הכלים דעשר ספירות דאצילות הן כח הגבול,
phrases.en: really, even the vessels of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are only a potential limitation,

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.en: not an actual limitation.

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: רק כאשר האור ושפע נגבל מאין ליש בבי''ע, אז נקרא גבול בפועל ממש וכמו שיתבאר בעזרת השם)
phrases.en: only when the *kelim* of *Atzilus* actually do something in *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* is it considered a *gvul b'poel*.

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **Really, even the vessels of the ten sefiros of Atzilus are only a potential limitation, not an actual limitation.** **Only when the kelim of Atzilus actually do something in Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya is it considered a gvul b'poel.** As with the soul in the body: only when you actually think, say, throw or do something is that an actual limit. Your hand has a certain range of motion, but right now, when you are not trying to move, it is not limiting you, so it is a *gvul b'koach* (a limit in potential): you have only the *etzem* and the *mahus*. When it moves, you have the *metzius* (existence), coming out in a certain, circumstantial way.

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text:
What did we say until now? Chapters 27 and 28 gave the general idea of lights and vessels. Then: when you are *misbonen* (contemplating) on them, the main point is *ihu v'chayohi chad*, *ihu v'garmohi chad*: *Hashem* is one with the light and with the vessel equally, both directly from His choice.

To understand that, we explained *gvul b'koach* and *gvul b'poel*. Your arm, with your soul in your body, has a power to move only a certain way, but it does not force you into any one movement; within that range you choose whatever you want, so it is still called infinite, only within a certain context. An actual limitation is when you actually throw something: you did it the way you did it. All this comes from the *kav hamida*, the way He chooses. Then we explained the *kavanos* (intentions), that you can be *mechaven* (have in mind) the light or the vessel.

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: The lights come from the *Kav* and the vessels from the *reshimu*, and both come from their one source, G-d's choice. The vessels of *Atzilus* that actually limit, the names *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*, called letters, are only a *gvul b'koach*. So the actual limitation that comes through them is chosen by G-d. His creative power, the light of *chesed*, goes into the vessel of *chesed* and through it into *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, but not like a machine or a function, where the light goes in and the world comes out automatically. How it comes out through the vessels is also His choice. That is why He is one with the vessels: they are controlled by G-d, "not a machine."

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: "This is the big statement. We are officially making this controversial proclamation against common belief or whatever." Not really controversial; nobody passionately believes otherwise. But most people picture the *hishtalshelus* as a machine, a mechanistic thing. The main thing to realize: though there are vessels, limited, *chachma* and *bina* (understanding), the vessels of *Atzilus*, they are not machines. G-d chooses how and when to use them.

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

phrases.he: הרי זה עצמו הכוונה במקור השמות דע''ב ס''ג כו',

phrases.en: that the source of the names *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH*, *BaN* is the source of the light of *Atzilus* actually.

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **And based on this, when somebody's mechaven different names**: you *daven* *Shemoneh Esrei* with the *kavanos* of the Arizal (Rabbi Isaac Luria), this blessing in *chesed* and this one in *gevura*, the names **which are the vessels that actually limit**. Thinking of the particular way G-d's *chesed* came out, **really you're being mechaven to the source, the one that chose to use it and do it in that way.**

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: Recognizing that G-d does it, you can look at it two ways: "G-d is so nice, He's so kind," or focus on what He did, "G-d gave me money," which is the vessel. But once you recognize that He did not have to and chose to give it to you, you are not thinking about the vessel. You are thinking about Him, the one behind the vessel.

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: With a person that is obvious. But people ask, "Well, what are you *mechaven* to, the *chesed*?", as if to the *sefira*. That is why you are not supposed to be *mechaven* the *kavanos* of the Arizal unless you understand them: otherwise you will think it is a machine, that you are davening to *chesed* and *gevura*. If you understand what is going on, those *kavanos* themselves help you be *mechaven* to *Hashem*.

blocks.text: This is on the level of *pshat* (the plain meaning) too. Saying G-d brings the rain, blows the wind and makes the grass grow does not say that He is a force that makes the wind blow. blocks.text: **The source of the names Ayin Beis, SaG, MaH, BaN is the source of the light of Atzilus actually**: the light G-d reveals through the vessels comes from the same source as the vessels. Seeing past them to the source, the *kavana* in the vessels is not lesser than the *kavana* in the light; it is the same *kavana*. Some places say to be *mechaven* to the light in the vessel, not to the vessel; they all really say that you should be talking to G-d.

blocks.text: So if you just want to talk to G-d, why use different names and *kavanos*? Because you are supposed to recognize what He does for you. You call Him King, so recognize how G-d rules the world and controls everything, how He is kind, and what good things He does for you. That is part of this *kavana*.

blocks.title: A name and a title
blocks.text:
**The real thing of Shem Havaya** (the four-letter Name) **is really the shem ha'etzem** (the proper name), **that's G-d's name.** Some names are titles: father, son, doctor, teacher. Then there is your name: "your name is Shmuel. That's just your name." Shmuel also means something, "G-d listened to my prayer": Chana's prayer for a child was answered. So in a way it is a title, but that is not the main thing: it is just who you are.

The same with *Havaya*: it connotes *haya hoveh v'yihyeh* (He was, He is and He will be), and *mehaveh*, constantly creating, but that is not the real idea. It is just G-d's name, like "G-d" in English.

blocks.title: The painting and the gift
blocks.text: **Because the actual limitation connects with the potential limitation, that makes the limitation in the actual limitation.** You paint a painting, and we say, "Look, you painted that": it reflects your artistic ability. You give somebody money, and we say, "Look how nice you are," because you did not have to and you chose to. What comes out is an actual thing separate from you and still a revelation of you, because it is according to your ability and your choice of how to use it.

audio.lecture: 60 - Chap- 29-4 Gvul biKoach and Gvul biPoel.mp3

blocks.text: **Like power of movement in your hand, which connects to the actual movement that you make**: you control your body. If you go punch somebody, you exercised your hand's ability to move and decided to do it, and that is why you are responsible for what you do.

blocks.text: Someone not in control of his body is not responsible. A sleeper who breaks something that he knew was next to his bed is responsible; if it was put there after he fell asleep, he is not. A guy totally drunk is not responsible, because he did not know what he was doing. But if you know what you are doing, the deed is connected to you, so you are responsible: it reflects on you.

sections.summary: As they are revealed, the *tzimtzum* is in the lights and the spreading is in the vessels, as a teacher's many words reveal more by limiting the idea. blocks.title: The teacher's many words
blocks.text: The more words a teacher says, the better the students understand. "Not necessarily, I mean, not if he's wasting words"; but the more he explains, the more intellect he gives them. blocks.title: The idea and the words
blocks.text: From the teacher's point of view, the light is infinite, a big revelation, and the vessels are a very big limitation, because he has to work within the system. Explaining something, you see the idea, and the language you have to express it in limits it; it is hard to fit it in. But once you fit it in, the more words you say, the more it is revealed to the recipient.

blocks.text: And this is why, when you face somebody, your right hand faces his left hand: what is *chesed* for the *mashpia* (the giver) is *gevura* for the *mekabel* (the receiver), and what is *gevura* for the *mashpia* is *chesed* for the *mekabel*.

blocks.title: The Rebbe in his room
blocks.text: Take the Rebbe. When he comes out with many *sichos* and *maamarim* (talks and discourses), we say, "Oh, look, it's a big *gilui*, a big *chesed*"; when he stays in his room, "a big *gevura*, a big *helem*," concealment. For the Rebbe it is the opposite: in his room he is himself, a much bigger *chesed*. Coming out, he has to be *metzamtzem* himself "to explain things in a very stupid way to us", "and say little jokes", the same thing over and over "because they don't get it." There is a *chiddush* (new insight) each time, but next to his level it is "so ridiculous, such a limitation."

blocks.text: So it really switches. In a way the actual revelation we get is from the *tzimtzum*: our main *gilui* of G-d is the way He chooses the vessels, limiting Himself to reveal Himself in a way we can appreciate. The source shows only the power of limit, which in a way is a more limited thing.
